title: Onboarding For Apps That Have Nothing to Say Yet
summary: Before a user has done anything inside your app, you already have a handful of usable datapoints to leverage for retention.
body_markdown:
### You know more on day one than it feels like


Every mobile app marketing team eventually hits the same wall on day one: you're supposed to[personalize app onboarding](https://onesignal.com/blog/how-to-build-an-effective-mobile-app-onboarding-process/) , **but there's nothing to personalize with yet** . No purchase history. No behavioral pattern. No idea if this user even likes your product, because they downloaded it eleven minutes ago. So you do the thing everyone does: write one generic welcome message, send it to everyone, and promise yourself you'll "add personalization later, once you have the data."


But "later" is expensive. Apps that wait to personalize until they've built up enough history are leaving retention on the table during the exact window when new users are most likely to[churn](https://onesignal.com/blog/your-churn-signals-are-pointing-at-the-wrong-customers/) . And the good news is that you don't need much data to do meaningfully better than a generic blast. You just need to stop treating "no personalization data" and "no signal at all" as the same thing, because they're not.


Before a user has done anything inside your app, you already have a handful of usable facts:


- Where they came from (an ad, a referral link, an App Store search, a specific promo code)
- What platform they're on (iOS and Android often behave differently)
- Whether they granted push permission, and when
- What screen or action, if any, they touched in their first session
- The time of day and day of week they signed up


You can capture these signals when a user opens the app, without waiting for a data warehouse. Use them to create two or three onboarding paths: for example, send users who viewed a key screen a[deep link back to that screen](https://onesignal.com/blog/deep-linking-best-practices/) , while users who did not reach it receive a message that explains the next step. Measure each path by completion of the first key action and return sessions.


### The best retention tactics post-install don't wait for a data model


Send onboarding messages early through more than one channel. Apps that use more than one onboarding channel see higher 1-day, 7-day, and 30-day retention than apps that use one channel. Per[OneSignal's State of Customer Engagement Report](https://onesignal.com/the-2024-state-of-customer-engagement-report) , **apps that send onboarding messages report a 56.25% higher DAU/MAU ratio and 24% higher install-to-purchase conversion** . These tactics can start without a detailed behavioral profile.


A great example is a[UK sports betting app](https://onesignal.com/case-studies/betmate) that used each user's promo code or signup offer to create referral-specific onboarding sequences. Founder Ryan Lawrence says[automated Journeys](https://onesignal.com/journeys) tailors each experience to the user's acquisition source. That day-one signal helped **drive a 30% increase in new-user deposits** .


### Where AI actually earns its place in this


[Autonomous lifecycle marketing](https://onesignal.com/blog/the-future-of-lifecycle-marketing-is-autonomous/) can start on day one. Use the signals available at install, including acquisition source, platform, permission status, first action, and signup timing, to define segments and branch a welcome journey. AI can help turn those inputs into journey logic without requiring years of behavioral history or separate versions for every audience.


For post-install retention, build initial segments from day-one signals and use[plain-language AI assistance](https://onesignal.com/ai) to draft the Journey logic. A small team can then branch push, in-app, or email messages based on each user's actions, deep-link users to the next relevant screen, and measure return engagement as behavioral data grows.


### A few proven moves, in order of effort


**Start onboarding on two channels** . At signup, record the user's platform, notification permission status, and acquisition source as Data Tags. Use those tags to start a two-step Journey: send a push at signup confirmation, then send an in-app message or email 24 hours later if the user has not reopened the app. For a fitness app, the follow-up can point to the first workout, goal, or feature the user needs to try next.


**Branch by source, not behavior** . Referral users, paid-ad users, and organic sign-ups all deserve a different first message. That data already exists. Step one: tag users by referral source or promo code at signup using a Data Tag, then build two or three segments instead of trying to build behavior-based ones you don't have data for yet. A fintech app with a referral program could reference the specific friend and bonus tied to a referral code, while organic sign-ups get a more general "here's what to explore first" message. Same platform, different first impression, based entirely on where they came from.


**Catch early drop-off with something visual** . Ogun added a carousel-style in-app onboarding flow and saw an[80% jump in click-through rate](https://onesignal.com/case-studies/ogun-case-study) , just from making the "what does this app even do" moment clearer. Step one: find the single screen where most users stall, usually a permissions prompt or account setup, and replace the wall of text with a short 3 to 5 screen carousel that shows rather than explains. If half your users bail right after the notification permission prompt, a quick carousel showing what they'd actually get by enabling it, shown before you ask, can recover a real chunk of that drop-off.


**Nudge toward the first real action, automatically** . Define what the first meaningful action is for your app (completed profile, first booking, first message sent) and set an automated reminder if it hasn't happened within 24 to 48 hours. A marketplace app might trigger a nudge referencing the exact listing someone browsed but never messaged about, rather than a generic "come back!" push.


**Don't skip the reactivation window, even early** . letgo's welcome campaign alone[onboarded 1.3 million new users at a 7% CTR](https://onesignal.com/case-studies/letgo) . Timing and relevance did the work, not deep personalization. Step one: pick a short inactivity window, 3 to 5 days for a high-frequency app is reasonable even with zero historical data, and set up one automated re-engagement message for anyone who installed and disappeared. You don't need to know exactly when someone's about to churn. You just need to catch them before they forget your app exists.


### Retention Starts From Day One


Use first-day signals, such as acquisition source, platform, permission status, first screen viewed, and signup timing, to tailor onboarding across channels. As users engage, update the audience and message path with the data they provide.
